epics.title: Cypher — the DeepSeek harness as a mind in the hive
epics.description:
The builder slot in the rebuild runner has only ever held two scripted controls. What goes in it is Cypher: a mind running the DeepSeek harness (dsh, checked out at /home/daniel/Storage/Dev/deepseek-harness, pinned at 47f9438), driving a small local model, in a container that can see almost nothing. The harness work itself — the resume module, the hooks bridge, the skills root, the provider shape — is its own feature. This epic is Cypher: the mind that runs it, what she can see, and what the referee records about her.

She is a mind rather than a subprocess because that is what the hive already knows how to do. Registration, the session token, the broker row, the host report and the model catalogue all come from being a mind; none of it gets reinvented to run a builder.

What is being measured, and when: the first several nights are not about how well an app gets built. They are about whether the harness can execute what the model hands it at all — a thirty-billion-parameter model emits a tool call, and either dsh can parse and run it or it cannot. The behaviour score will sit at zero through that, and the zero will mean nothing. The tool traffic is the measurement. Only once the traffic is boringly near perfect does the behaviour score become the headline, and only then is it worth letting the harness see the oracle's verdict and try again.
epics.requirements:
Where she lives: Cypher is a mind in the hive, declared the way the others are — one tracked harness module minds/harness/dsh_cli.py in the hive_mind repo, selected by her own container fragment and pointed at her own runtime.yaml through MIND_NAME, with no per-mind copy of the adapter. She mounts her own mind folder and one playground directory under Dev and nothing else; every other mind mounts the whole of Dev, but this one is the thing being trained to write code unsupervised overnight, so what it cannot see is the point. The playground is mounted at the same absolute path inside the container as outside it, because the brief names absolute paths, the attempt tree is written by Cypher and started by the referee on the host, and a path that means two different things on the two sides of that handoff is a score that cannot be trusted. Her harness configuration lives in her own mind folder as DSH_HOME, the same way the Claude and Codex minds keep their own config directories; no mind reads another's and none reads the host's.

The adapter: one dsh --profile headless process per turn, where the headless bundle takes one task, submits it as an ordinary user message, waits for quiescence, prints the last non-empty assistant text, and exits zero when the turn completed and one otherwise — that exit code is the turn's own verdict and is not interpreted as anything else. The model is never defaulted by the adapter; it comes from her runtime.yaml like every other mind's and a spawn without one is refused rather than quietly given a house favourite. The model is reached through the inference proxy and never as a bare daemon: a custom provider in her own settings.yaml, api: openai-completions, the proxy's base URL, the key from an environment variable, and qwen3.8 as the model — the proxy answers 401 without a bearer key, so the key is declared unconditionally rather than only when one happens to be visible. Every turn records its tool traffic: how many calls the model emitted, how many dsh could parse, how many it executed, how many it refused, and how many raised inside the tool, read out of dsh's own event stream rather than inferred from the text it printed. This is the first phase's only real metric and it has to come from the adapter because nothing outside the container can see it. A turn that ends with nothing executed is reported as such, distinctly from a turn that executed work and achieved little — in the first phase the former is the common case, and folding the two together makes a harness that never started look like a model that built badly. A turn continues the conversation it was given, and nothing here starts until the resume module exists in both halves: continue a session by the id it is handed, and create one under an id it did not mint. Every spawn carries the gateway's conversation id, and a harness that quietly starts a fresh conversation because it could not find the one it was given is how a week of context disappears without a single error; the codex pattern — dsh mints its own thread id, reports it, and the gateway persists it as harness_sid — is the fallback if session identity upstream will not take an outside id, not the target. The turn's result comes back as data: the session it ran in, why it stopped, and any error code.

Context: the served context window is declared explicitly, never inherited — the model carries 262,144 tokens natively and Ollama serves a fraction of that unless told otherwise, so an undeclared window is a harness that looks brain-damaged for a reason that has nothing to do with the harness. dsh's own compaction is off in round one: it is a summarizer whose priorities we cannot inspect, and a run being measured for tool traffic must not have its history silently rewritten by something we did not write; a run that hits the context ceiling records that as its outcome, which is the measurement that tells us what a carry-forward has to preserve. Round two replaces it rather than trusting it, because compaction in dsh is a seam — a service definition whose backend compaction-basic merely registers — so our own backend plugs into the same seam in our own profile with no fork and no patch to their code.

What is not in round one: skills, an orchestrator skill, subagents, memory hooks and rotation hooks are all out. Round one is one submitted task — here is the brief, build it — and the tool traffic is read off the result. One task is not one model call: inside a headless task the agent loops model call, tool call, result, again, until it goes quiet, so a single turn is an agentic run that can make hundreds of calls and an app is plausibly attemptable in one. Copying this mind's hooks wholesale from the operator mind would actively hurt it — those hooks serve a mind with a person on the other end and a soul in a graph, and the memory ones would inject another mind's recollections into a builder's context and contaminate both the run and the training signal.
epics.acceptance_criteria: The referee side: the runner's builder seam dispatches the brief to Cypher and waits for her turn to end. The referee stays on the host — it creates the attempt tree, starts what was built, runs the walkthrough and writes the ledger, and none of those are things the thing being measured may do. Attempt trees live under the playground, because that is the one directory both sides can see. The ledger carries the tool traffic beside the score, and an attempt where nothing was executed is its own outcome rather than a score of zero; the morning report leads with the traffic while the score is still zero. One pass per attempt: the harness builds, the referee scores, and that is the attempt. Letting the harness see the verdict and try again is the next phase and is capped at two or three scored rounds when it arrives — few enough that each round has to be a real build, because the oracle names the element identifiers it checks and a small model under pressure will learn to make those exist rather than make the app work.
epics.qa_tests: Phase one's measurement is tool traffic read from dsh's own event stream, not a behaviour score. The distinction that matters most: a turn that executed nothing is reported distinctly from a turn that executed work and achieved little, because folding them together makes a harness that never started look like a model that built badly. Round one's context ceiling is itself a measurement — a run that hits it records that as its outcome rather than having its history rewritten.

features.title: Cypher gets the hooks and skills a mind needs
features.description:
Cypher runs dsh. She has a tmux pane, a rotation, a Telegram surface and the hive's memory on her network, and none of the per-turn machinery every other mind has. This is the port.

How it is wired: dsh's own hooks-claude-code bridge translates a Claude-dialect settings file onto dsh's typed interception points — agent/session-start, agent/pre-step, tools/pre-execute, tools/post-execute, agent/turn-stopping, subagent/start, subagent/end. The bridge is not loaded in the hive bundle today; it gets inserted there, configured against a settings file in her DSH_HOME. One dialect, shell scripts, portable to every mind we stand up. The bridge carries no background_tasks, which the rotation fire gate reads — dsh has the data, JobRegistry.list(caller) on the context, the same registry tool-jobs exposes to the model, so the bridge's payload base is widened to emit it in the shape the existing hooks already parse, on Stop, SubagentStop and UserPromptSubmit. Claude Code offers it only on the first two, which is the entire reason bg_snapshot.sh writes it to disk for the fire hook to read back; on dsh the fire hook reads it live, taking the field when present and falling back to the snapshot file when absent, so one script serves both harnesses. Her transcript is not Claude's: dsh persists session.jsonl.zstd — zstd frames over jsonl, events typed session, user/message, assistant/message, tool/call, tool/result, step/start, step/end — so every hook that reads a transcript needs a reader for that format rather than a copy of the Claude one.

The spec grill found that the spec as first written ships a no-op. All three reviewers agreed. The surviving findings are carried as stories below, and the consequence is three pieces of work rather than one: hive_mind's seed path (now shipped), the dsh side, and the hooks themselves — which are not copies.
features.requirements:
The eleven requirements stand. 1: Cypher runs hook scripts of her own, from her own config home, and editing one of hers never touches anyone else's copy. 2: a turn arriving in one of her conversations carries the current time, the surface it came from, and the memories the hive holds that bear on it. 3: a turn arriving on a surface that speaks her reply aloud carries the spoken-output rule; one on a surface that does not, does not. 4: when one of her turns finishes, what was said is captured into the hive's memory under her own identity. 5: when one of her conversations nears its context limit it rotates, and her pane keeps its session, its name and its history across the rotation. 6: a rotation never fires while she has background work running. 7: a conversation she is typing into never stalls waiting on a hook. 8: a hook that fails, times out, or cannot reach the gateway costs its own effect and nothing else — the turn still lands. 9: she has the skills a mind needs — self-reflect, remember, always-remember, memory, save-session, end-session, rotate-session. 10: she has the skills the work she actually does needs, and a skill whose dependencies her container does not carry is named rather than installed broken. 11: all of it holds whichever model is answering her turn.

Assumptions recorded for want of an answer: requirement 4 is taken as yes, she writes per-turn captures to lucent under her own mind_id alongside every other mind's. Requirement 10 is read as every skill whose dependencies exist in her container, excluded on capability rather than preference, and the gap is listed so it is visible — restart-service and anything else needing the Docker socket, arnold-zack-bots with no SSH credential, cad-headless with no FreeCAD in the image, home-assistant with no HA token in her environment. Skippy's own telemetry-derived skills (auto-read-md-edit-sh-git, auto-sh-cat-set, auto-sh-echo-git) are not ported.
features.acceptance_criteria:
The four original tests do not stand. Three of them either pass against a constant, duplicate a test that already exists, or pin an oracle that is wrong for this format; they are redrawn with the work below. What remains testable: a Stop payload built in a context whose job registry reports running work carries that work as background_tasks, and carries an empty list where the registry reports none; a UserPromptSubmit payload carries the same field, which is the addition Claude Code does not offer and the one the fire gate reads live; reading a real dsh session file returns the user and assistant turns in the order they happened and leaves the tool, step and chunk events out; and the fire gate holds a staged rotation when the payload names running background work, holds it when the payload carries no such field but the snapshot file on disk names some, and lets it fire when neither does.

Not reachable by a test, verified by running it instead: requirement 11, because no code decides which model answers her turn — the proxy does — so it is verified by running her on two. The bundle loading the bridge at all and her settings file being found are configuration, verified by booting her and watching a hook fire. Her hook scripts and her skills: the scripts are copies whose only new code is the transcript reader, and the skills are markdown. Requirement 3's surface split, because the script that decides it is unchanged code already in service.
features.qa_tests:
Where the code lands: the bridge widening and the two payload tests in packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/ in the dsh tree, which has its own vitest suite; the dsh transcript reader and its test in minds/harness/ in hive_mind, tracked beside dsh_cli.py because every dsh mind needs it and minds/*/ is gitignored; and the fire-gate test against the gate itself, which is shared by both harnesses.

One trap to design the fixture around: the real session files are multi-frame zstd, one frame per append — 358 and 1988 frames on two of hers. A fixture compressed in one call is single-frame and would pass against a reader that decodes only the first frame, which on a real file yields the header line alone.

stories.title: Forward user_prompt and honour an opening user turn in pty_attach.py
stories.description: SHIPPED. hive-mind PR 286 and dsh PR 38, both merged to master and the dsh library rebuilt — it runs the compiled lib/, which is gitignored, so the merge alone changed nothing at runtime. 1235 passing in the main suite, 398 in comms, 113 in the dsh bundle. The bug: comms sends the staged seed as user_prompt, and minds/pty_attach.py forwarded only system_prompt and dropped it, because user_prompt and as_user_turn exist only in the edge repo. A fired rotation respawned the pane with an empty seed file and reported success, with the carry-forward and the user's typed message both gone. Every containerised mind with a terminal had this.
stories.requirements: Forward user_prompt and honour an opening user turn, so a containerised mind's rotation can carry anything at all.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A fired rotation in a container mind's pane carries its seed.
stories.qa_tests: Covered by the three suites named above.

stories.title: Stop the delivered seed being captured as something the operator said
stories.description: A finding from the grill that is not fixed and belongs to the hooks. Moving the seed to a positional user turn is the point of the change, and the consequence is that the seed now lands in the transcript — which is what makes the successor answer it. auto_remember.sh reads the last type == "user" entry, and on a successor's first turn that entry is the delivered seed: soul, decay-weighted recent memory, the rotation summary and the last exchange, up to 120,000 bytes. That text goes to the Ollama extractor and whatever it makes of it is written into the hive's knowledge graph as something the operator said this turn. Every terminal rotation therefore feeds the mind's own memory back into its memory, and it compounds. This is LIVE FOR SKIPPY TODAY — the bare-metal template already delivered the seed as a user turn — and is now live for every containerised mind too.
stories.requirements: Either the seed is delivered wrapped in a tag the hook skips, the way a surface block is, or the hook learns to recognise a turn whose source is the gateway. The second is better — a tag in the text is a tag the model reads — but it needs something on the transcript entry to key on.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A successor's first turn does not write the seed into the knowledge graph as operator speech.
stories.qa_tests: Rotate a terminal and inspect what the capture hook wrote for the successor's first turn: it must not be the seed. The compounding is the thing to check for across two rotations, not one.

stories.title: Package the hooks bridge and load it from Cypher's own profile layer
stories.description: The hive bundle patch is shared by every dsh mind and the host's own dsh, and Cypher mounts the whole dsh tree read-only — a bridge row there is one hooks file for all of them. Her own per-mind layer, minds/cypher/.dsh/profiles/hive/cordis.patch.yml, is on the writable mount and is currently empty; that is the place. And @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code is a dependency of no bundle and is installed in neither her profile's node_modules nor the CLI's, so this is a packaging change, not a configuration line.
stories.requirements: Package the bridge as a real dependency and load it from her own profile layer rather than the shared bundle patch.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A hook fires for Cypher and no other dsh install is affected.
stories.qa_tests: Boot her and watch a hook fire — this is configuration, not code, so it is verified by running it. Confirm the host's own dsh and another dsh mind are unchanged.

stories.title: Add zstd to Cypher's image
stories.description: Her transcripts are zstd-framed jsonl and nothing in her image can read them.
stories.requirements: zstd available in the container.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A transcript read succeeds inside the container.
stories.qa_tests: Reading a real multi-frame session file inside the container returns every frame, not just the first.

stories.title: Widen the bridge payload to carry the job registry on three events
stories.description: dsh has the data — JobRegistry.list(caller) on the context — in the shape the existing hooks already parse. Widening base() emits the field on all seven events including every tool call; widening the base and scoping to three events are different changes, and it is the second that is wanted: Stop, SubagentStop and UserPromptSubmit.
stories.requirements: The field on exactly those three events. Four correctness problems to fix with it: JobRegistry.list(caller) is fenced by owner session and background bash and background subagents are owned by the parent, while SubagentStop builds its payload from the child — so it would report an empty list at exactly the moment the gate exists for, and bg_snapshot would key its file under a session id the fire hook never reads. JobStatus includes stopping — kill requested, process group still up — and the existing filter keeps only running, so a draining job reads as nothing running and the respawn takes it. Settled jobs stay in the registry until owner disposal, so the steady state is a list full of completed entries rather than an empty list. And JobSnapshot carries kind and label while the Python side reads type, description and command, so unmapped, the message that holds a rotation names nothing.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A Stop payload in a context with running work carries it; with none, it carries an empty list. A UserPromptSubmit payload carries the same field.
stories.qa_tests: In the dsh tree's own vitest suite. A payload built against a registry reporting a draining (stopping) job must report work running — that is the case the current filter gets wrong and the respawn would kill. A SubagentStop payload must report the parent's jobs, not the child's empty list.

stories.title: Pass a message's source through the bridge so the fire gate can tell a typed message from a job notice
stories.description: _is_typed recognises Claude's envelope tags. dsh delivers a finished job as a plain-prose follow-up, so the gate reads it as typed and the pane rotates itself with nobody there. dsh does carry the signal — the message's source is {kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'tool-jobs', form: 'notice'} — and promptPayload discards it by flattening to text.
stories.requirements: The bridge passes the source through; the fire gate keys on it.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A job notice does not fire a rotation.
stories.qa_tests: A payload whose source names the tool-jobs plugin does not fire. One from a real typed message does. This is the exact failure mode where the successor opens on notification XML with nobody at the keyboard.

stories.title: Write a dsh transcript reader that counts tokens correctly
stories.description: rotation_check._live_context_tokens reads message.usage with input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens and output_tokens. dsh nests it at data.usage and names them inputTokens, outputTokens and cacheReadTokens. No usage is found, so it falls through to dividing the COMPRESSED byte count by a chars-per-token constant — measured on a real session at 295,256 against a true live context near 131,072. cacheReadTokens dominates the real figure (97,120 of 98,525 on one turn), so summing input and output under-reads by seventy times. Many assistant/message entries carry usage of all zeros, which the Claude hook already guards for its own synthetic entries and a new reader would not. dsh also prunes its own context through compaction/prune, so turns that happened and turns still in context are different sets.
stories.requirements: Count from data.usage including cacheReadTokens, guard the all-zeros entries, and respect compaction/prune so the count reflects what is still in context.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The counted figure tracks the true live context rather than the compressed byte count.
stories.qa_tests: Against a real session file: the count is near the true live context, not seventy times under or twice over. An all-zeros usage entry does not zero the running figure. A session with pruned turns counts what remains, not what happened.

stories.title: Filter the transcript reader on source.kind so system reminders are not read as operator speech
stories.description: Of 39 user/message events in one real session, 8 have source.kind == "user". The rest are system-prompt snapshots, skill catalogues, goal revisions and subagent reports. A reader meeting the original test as written hands a system reminder back as something the operator said, which requirement 4 then writes to lucent in her name.
stories.requirements: Only genuine user messages are returned as user turns.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A system-prompt snapshot is never reported as operator speech.
stories.qa_tests: Against the real session with 39 user/message events: the reader returns the 8 with source.kind == "user" and none of the other 31. Tool, step and chunk events are absent. The fixture must be multi-frame zstd, because a single-frame fixture passes against a reader that only decodes the first frame.

stories.title: Give the hooks one writable state root
stories.description: rotation_state.state_dir() resolves $HIVE_PROJECT_DIR/data/auto-remember, which is /usr/src/app/data/auto-remember — a read-only mount. mkdir fails, stage_marker returns False, rotation_check discards that return and reports STAGED anyway, and the fire hook finds no marker on every turn. Both diagnostic logs are inside the same unwritable directory. rotation_check roots its log at SKIPPY_PROJECT_ROOT, rotation_state at HIVE_PROJECT_DIR, and auto_remember.sh at AUTO_REMEMBER_LOG_DIR; in her container all three resolve somewhere absent or unwritable. That is the exact failure rotation_state's own docstring predicts.
stories.requirements: The one writable path is /usr/src/app/minds/cypher, and the three variables have to become one.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A staged marker is written and found, and rotation_check does not report STAGED on a failed write.
stories.qa_tests: stage_marker's return value is honoured rather than discarded — a failed write must not report STAGED. The marker written by one hook process is found by the next. All three logs land in one writable place.

stories.title: Guard the hooks against delegate sessions
stories.description: Her sessions run 128 at depth one, 4 at depth two, 1 at depth three, against 57 at depth zero. The bridge registers on its root context, so every delegate fires SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and Stop with its own session id. Unguarded, that writes each delegate's turn into lucent as hers and runs a multi-minute composition per delegate Stop. The repo already states the rule for the voice tailer — only blocks with no agent are the mind's own — and there is no analogue here.
stories.requirements: A delegate's turns are not captured as the mind's own, and a delegate Stop does not trigger a rotation composition.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Only depth-zero turns reach lucent under her identity.
stories.qa_tests: A delegate's Stop writes nothing to lucent and starts no composition. Her own turn does both. With 128 delegates at depth one in a real session, the unguarded case is 128 multi-minute compositions, which is the cost to measure against.

stories.title: Rewrite the capture script for the dsh transcript format
stories.description: auto_remember.sh extracts inline with jq against .type == "user" and .message.content[]. dsh writes user/message with data.content[] inside a zstd container, so the capture is empty and the script logs a skip. A bash pipeline cannot call a Python reader, so that script is a rewrite rather than a patch.
stories.requirements: A capture path that reads the dsh format, filters on source.kind, and writes under her own mind_id.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A turn of hers is captured into lucent under her identity.
stories.qa_tests: A real turn produces a lucent row carrying her UUID. A session where the script currently logs a skip produces a row. Confirm the row is her content and not a system reminder.

stories.title: Make the rotation threshold model-aware on dsh
stories.description: _threshold_for_model branches on a model family it reads from message.model and from a --model argv. dsh writes neither; the model travels as DSH_MODEL. Every conversation gets the default threshold.
stories.requirements: Read the model from DSH_MODEL so the threshold matches the model actually answering.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A conversation on a large-window model is not rotated at the small-window threshold.
stories.qa_tests: Two models with different windows produce different thresholds. Today both get the default, which is the failure.

stories.title: Fix the empty transcript_path firing an unmeasured rotation
stories.description: transcript_path is '' rather than absent when persistence is unmounted, and rotation_fire._still_over_threshold answers true on that path — firing a rotation it never measured.
stories.requirements: An empty path is treated as absent, and an unmeasured threshold does not read as over.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A rotation never fires on a measurement that did not happen.
stories.qa_tests: With transcript_path empty, _still_over_threshold answers false. With a real path over the threshold, true. The dangerous case is the first, because it fires silently.

stories.title: Reconcile hook timing with requirement 7
stories.description: runPoint runs hooks serially where Claude Code parallelises matcher groups, and Skippy's own registration allows the fire hook 320 seconds on the prompt-gating path. Requirement 7 — a conversation she is typing into never stalls waiting on a hook — contradicts the config being copied.
stories.requirements: The registered timings have to be consistent with never stalling a typed prompt on dsh's serial execution.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A typed message is never held while a hook runs long.
stories.qa_tests: A hook made to run long does not hold the prompt. UserPromptSubmit gates submission, so every second in that hook is a second the pane sits frozen with the message unsent and nothing on screen saying why.

stories.title: Make exit code 2 from a hook not discard the user's turn
stories.description: Exit code 2 from any hook maps to a block and discards the user's turn, so requirement 8 holds for crashes and timeouts but not for exit 2.
stories.requirements: A hook exiting 2 costs its own effect and nothing else.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The turn still lands.
stories.qa_tests: A hook exiting 2 leaves the turn delivered. A hook crashing or timing out already does; this closes the third case.

stories.title: Stamp HIVE_SURFACE on chat turns, not only on the pane path
stories.description: HIVE_SURFACE is set only on the pane path, in all three adapters. The chat spawn stamps OWNER_TYPE instead, and nothing in hive_mind derives the surface from it — that line exists only in the edge repo. So requirement 2 carries no surface on her Telegram turns and requirement 3's split never happens; a headless build run gets the spoken-output rule because unset falls through to 'spoken'.
stories.requirements: Every spawn carries the surface, chat included.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A Telegram turn carries telegram and a headless build run does not get the spoken-output rule.
stories.qa_tests: A Telegram turn's payload names its surface. A headless run's does too, and the prose rule does not fire on it. Unset falling through to spoken is the current behaviour and the thing to eliminate.

stories.title: Handle a turn that errors running no Stop hook
stories.description: agent/turn-stopping is dispatched inside the try block; an error sets the turn's end without dispatching. Her transcripts show this routinely — a 402 from the proxy, for one. The snapshot's freshness guarantee is that the last draining task produces a Stop carrying an empty list; on dsh that is false whenever the draining turn errors, and the rotation is held permanently while the model is told to say so on every message.
stories.requirements: An errored turn must not leave the rotation held forever.
stories.acceptance_criteria: A 402 from the proxy does not permanently wedge the rotation.
stories.qa_tests: A turn made to error leaves the gate in a state the next turn can clear. Today it holds permanently, which is the defect.

stories.title: Give Cypher's container an OLLAMA_URL
stories.description: Her container has no OLLAMA_URL in its environment, so remember, always-remember and the rotation composition would all resolve loopback inside the container and be refused. Ollama binds 127.0.0.1 on the host with the Host check on, and containers reach it through ollama-bridge-relay.service on the docker0 gateway.
stories.requirements: The variable is present and points at the relay, not at loopback.
stories.acceptance_criteria: The three memory paths reach a model.
stories.qa_tests: remember, always-remember and a rotation composition each reach a model from inside her container. Loopback inside a container is the failure this fixes.

stories.title: Establish where Cypher's mind skills come from
stories.description: self-reflect, memory and save-session are not in Skippy's user skills directory at all; they live in specs/skills/claude/ in the edge repo. The spec never said where the skills come from.
stories.requirements: A named source for each of the seven mind skills, and an install path from it.
stories.acceptance_criteria: All seven are installed and invocable.
stories.qa_tests: Each of the seven is present in her skills root and invocable. A skill sourced from nowhere is the gap this closes.

stories.title: Measure the skill exclusion list rather than asserting it
stories.description: cad-headless was excluded for a missing dependency that was asserted rather than measured. The exclusion list has to be measured.
stories.requirements: Each exclusion is backed by a check inside her container.
stories.acceptance_criteria: Every excluded skill is excluded on a measured capability gap.
stories.qa_tests: For each candidate skill, check its dependency inside the container. A skill excluded on an assumption that turns out false is a skill she should have had.
